research_objective: Create a defensible prospective pilot for the existing python skill dimension without claiming MG effectiveness before legitimate independent outcomes exist.

measurement_instrument.assessment_structure: 10-item Python assessment with one form for baseline and one parallel form for follow-up; each form includes tasks from variables_and_types, control_flow, functions, collections, debugging_reasoning, and problem_solving.
measurement_instrument.scoring_rule: Each objective item receives its maximum_points only when its expected value matches or its declared code contract passes all deterministic test cases. Raw score is the sum of earned item points.

mapping_to_aura_scale.transformation_rule: Each form has 10 items worth 10 points, so aura_python_skill equals raw_score directly; no post-hoc, data-dependent, or MG/base adjustment is applied.

measurement_instrument.baseline_measurement_method: Use deterministic counterbalanced assignment by stable participant/user ID hashing. Group AB: T0 = Form A and T1 = Form B. Group BA: T0 = Form B and T1 = Form A. Participants cannot choose the form.
measurement_instrument.followup_measurement_method: Use the assigned counterbalanced follow-up form for the participant. The protocol does not claim A/B equivalence; it only preserves blueprint matching and deterministic assignment.

parallel_forms.requirement: The protocol uses deterministic counterbalanced assignment across Form A and Form B with matched domain blueprint coverage only; equivalence is not assumed without later evidence.
parallel_forms.assignment_group_rule: Group AB = A then B; Group BA = B then A; assignment determined by a stable hash of user_id.

measurement_instrument.invalid_assessment_handling: Score must be rejected or converted into a missing outcome when the assessment is incomplete, invalid, or unverified.
measurement_instrument.assessment_validity_rule: Every required item completed; each submitted coding task executed using SECURE_CONTAINER and passed deterministic test cases; no scoring error; unique episode-linked evidence ID; bound form ID/version/hash; valid assignment/phase; timezone-aware timestamps within phase windows; verified raw score identity mapping; ASSESSMENT provenance only.
measurement_instrument.baseline_form: Form A or Form B depending on deterministic group assignment
measurement_instrument.followup_form: The alternated form from the same deterministic group assignment

score_transformation.deterministic_mapping: With 10 items worth 10 points each, aura_python_skill = raw_score. No normalization, data-dependent scaling, post-hoc adjustment, or prediction adjustment is applied.
score_transformation.scale_validity_note: The AURA 0-100 python skill scale remains an operational system scale; this pilot estimates operational usefulness, not psychometric external validity.

pilot_action.content_scope: Three required exercises across variables, loops, and functions, plus optional collections/debugging practice.
pilot_action.action_standardization_gap: Closed by versioned module manifest and exact required-exercise list.

population.description: Narrow, early-career or self-directed Python learners who are eligible for the agreed assessment and practice module.
inclusion_criteria: valid baseline python skill signal exists in AURA state schema
participant can complete the finalized assessment and practice module
participant consent and evidence capture are available
exclusion_criteria: no valid baseline python skill value
participant cannot complete the finalized action or assessment
assessment or action cannot be audited
withdrawal_criteria: participant become ineligible for the study action
evidence cannot be collected or audited

observation_horizon.primary_horizon_rationale: Seven days is a pragmatic feasibility horizon, not a proven psychometric optimum. It balances expected skill-change latency, follow-up reliability, and participant burden.
observation_horizon.external_confounding_risk: Seven-day windows allow real-world exposure to courses, tutorials, AI tools, or projects; these must be recorded as metadata rather than controlled away.

external_learning_metadata.note: These values are confounder descriptors and are not used to condition MG predictions or to define outcome values.

primary_endpoint.name: paired_delta_error
primary_endpoint.definition: delta_error = abs(observed_outcome - mg_prediction) - abs(observed_outcome - base_prediction); negative values favor MG on that episode.
primary_endpoint.aggregation_plan: Future confirmatory analysis will aggregate episode-level delta_error using a single pre-registered summary statistic; additional metrics remain secondary/exploratory.
primary_endpoint.status: FROZEN_FORMULA_ONLY; not calculated during this audit.

delta_min.policy: No numeric delta_min should be invented from synthetic data or a priori assumptions. Estimate the distribution of paired delta_error, paired-delta SD, measurement noise, missingness, and exclusion rate from a Stage A pilot, then freeze the final threshold before the confirmatory cohort.

sample_size_strategy.pilot_feasibility_sample: 30-50 valid episodes is a pragmatic target for estimating variance and protocol drift; it is not a powered cohort.
sample_size_strategy.status: PILOT_SAMPLE_ONLY; confirmatory sample size remains pending pilot variance estimation.

outcome_provenance.blinding_required: Outcome-entry staff should not see frozen base or MG predictions when practical; any unavoidable deviation must be documented.

audit_findings: The v1 assessment forms, blueprint, and practice module have content and integrity hashes, but are not owner-approved.
Code submissions are evaluated in a restricted-exec subprocess with timeout; Python introspection can escape the restrictions, so this is not a secure sandbox.
Assessment result creation does not yet enforce evidence ID, timestamp, assignment-phase, or provenance validation as a collection-ready lifecycle.
No numeric quality cutoff is used; required deterministic validity conditions are recorded in provenance_quality_policy.
The 7-day follow-up horizon is a pragmatic feasibility horizon, not a validated psychometric optimum.
No real outcomes should be collected until the execution isolation and evidence-validation blockers are resolved and human approval is recorded.
collection_blockers: submitted Python requires OS-level or equivalent isolation before real participants can provide code
assessment evidence ID, timestamps, form assignment, and provenance validity are not enforced end-to-end by a collection workflow
pilot owner approval is pending and must remain a human action
collection_ready remains false until all technical blockers are resolved and owner approval is recorded
protocol_version_hash_status: A deterministic SHA-256 digest is computed across the frozen protocol payload and must remain stable after each audit revision.

code_execution.secure_backend: DockerContainerExecutor requiring a digest-pinned worker image and passing runtime health check
code_execution.known_security_limit: The development restricted-exec subprocess is not a security sandbox; Python introspection may escape it. Real submissions are rejected unless the Docker secure backend is configured and healthy.

provenance_quality_policy.deterministic_validity_rule: assessment_valid = all required items completed AND coding tasks executed successfully AND evidence_id present AND form/version/hash valid AND timestamps valid AND score transformation verified

version_freeze_policy.before_owner_approval: v1 artifacts may be corrected during audit.
version_freeze_policy.subsequent_changes: Any later change requires a new v2 artifact; do not mutate an approved v1 in place.

remaining_blockers: The audit host has no Docker CLI/runtime and no digest-pinned secure worker image configured; participant code cannot run in the required isolated backend.
A complete valid secure-container-backed baseline-to-follow-up-to-outcome lifecycle remains unverified.
Pilot-owner approval remains a separate pending human action.
